answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by licensing one working windmill per identity, set on a named ridge where a willow-lined lane leads to the mill door. The miller grinds grain for real buyers, each sack sealed in umber ink by an independent inspector, and random checks summon the holder to grind live on camera within minutes, so one operator cannot tend two mills in the same wind. The license fee in outside money doubles per further identity on the same funding trail, so each extra fake costs another real windmill lease, another milling season, another human, and twice the prior fee.
